title: Australian federal migration law for skilled visas: the Migration Act 1958, the Migration Regulations 1994 and the Minister's instruments

laws.title: Migration Regulations 1994, Schedule 1 item 1137: Skilled—Independent (Permanent) (Class SI) visa, application charges, where and how to apply, and further requirements for each stream
laws.amendment: Amended by regulations the Governor-General makes under the Migration Act 1958. The first-instalment amounts in item 1137(3) and (4J) were changed by regulations commencing on 1 July in each year from 2023 to 2026: the Migration Amendment (Visa Application Charges) Regulations 2023, 2024 and 2025, then Schedule 3 of the Home Affairs Legislation Amendment (2026 Measures No. 1) Regulations 2026, which replaced (3) and (4J). pitfalls.text: The age limit is tested at the time of invitation: the primary applicant must not have turned 45 then (item 1137(4B), table item 3), and the points for age read the age at invitation too (Schedule 6D Part 6D.1, 15 points from 40 to under 45, none from 45). Part 189 sets no other age limit for the primary applicant, so turning 45 after the invitation does not bar the application.

A person attains an age at the start of the anniversary of the birth date (Acts Interpretation Act s 37A), which applies to the Regulations and instruments through s 13(1)(a) of the Legislation Act 2003. Section 37A does not say when someone born on 29 February has the anniversary in a common year; s 2G ends a period at the end of a month that lacks the start day, but no text read applies it to ages.

Each criterion has its own time. The skills assessment, competent English, the occupation list and the points of Schedule 6D Parts 6D.1 to 6D.10 are read at the time of invitation, while some partner items of Part 6D.11 state no time; the 12 months of a de facto relationship end immediately before the application; the second instalment looks at age 18 at the application; and the Part 189 note requires all criteria to be met at the time of decision. Points are given under the Regulations in force when the assessment is made (Migration Act s 93(2)).

Reaching the pass mark is not enough: the score must be at least the score stated in the invitation (clause 189.224(1)) and at least the qualifying score (189.224(2)). LIN 19/210 sets the pass mark and pool mark at 65 for subclass 189 applications made on or after 2019-11-16; its older marks apply only to applications made before then. In Schedule 6D only one item counts in each Part, the one giving the most points (reg 2.26AC(4)), and overseas and Australian employment together give at most 20 points (6D51).

Partner points in Part 6D.11 depend on whether the spouse or de facto partner applies too: 10 points if the principal has no partner or the partner is an Australian citizen or permanent resident; 10 if the partner applies for the same subclass, was under 45 when the invitation was issued, and at invitation had a listed occupation, a suitable skills assessment not for a subclass 485 visa and competent English; 5 if the partner applies and had competent English at invitation. A partner who does not apply gives none.

Only occupations on the Medium and Long-term Strategic Skills List of LIN 19/051 count for subclass 189, as the list stands when the invitation is issued (s 12 of the instrument, item 1137(4B) table item 4); the occupation must also be the one the invitation names. The relevant assessing authority is the one specified for the occupation. Some changes reach pending applications: items 1 and 3 of LIN 26/027 apply to applications made, but not finally determined, on or after 2025-10-08, except with a Surveyor assessment dated on or before 2025-08-21, and item 2 to those on or after 2024-12-14.

At invitation the skills assessment must be positive, not made for a subclass 485 visa, and either still within the validity period it states, when that period ends no more than 3 years after the assessment, or otherwise no more than 3 years old. An assessment based on a qualification obtained in Australia while on a student visa counts only if the course was a registered course.

Competent English needs a specified test taken in the 3 years before the invitation with the instrument's score in each of the 4 components, or citizenship of and a valid passport from Canada, New Zealand, Ireland, the United Kingdom or the United States. Scores differ by component: from 2025-08-07, IELTS 6 in each, PTE Academic 47 listening, 48 reading, 51 writing and 54 speaking. For a test taken before 2025-08-07 and in the 36 months before the visa application, s 10 of LIN 25/016 also accepts its own shorter list of tests and scores (PTE Academic 50 in each).

The second instalment of AUD 4,885 is due before grant for each applicant at least 18 at the application and assessed as not having functional English; the table does not exempt the primary applicant, and family violence cases under 189.311(3) to (5) pay nil. Evidence of functional English includes a listed test from the 12 months before the application or later (IELTS average 4.5, PTE Academic 24), schooling or Australian study in English, a 2-year award taught in English, citizenship and passport of the 5 countries, or an interview.

From 2026-07-01 the first instalment is AUD 6,135 base, 3,070 for each other applicant of 18 or more and 1,540 under 18, or AUD 5,030, 2,515 and 1,260 when the primary applicant holds a valid passport issued by one of the 13 Pacific-regional countries of reg 1.03, for the primary and the applications combined with theirs. The test is the primary applicant's valid passport, not citizenship, and not a family member's passport. The concession and its definition came with the Home Affairs Legislation Amendment (2026 Measures No. 1) Regulations 2026.

The first instalment is payable when the application is made, so the amounts in force on that day apply. From 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30 they were AUD 4,910, 2,455 and 1,230, with no Pacific-regional concession. The item 1137(3) amounts were changed by regulations commencing on 1 July in each year from 2023 to 2026. The second instalment of AUD 4,885 was not changed by those regulations.

Under reg 1.12(2)(b), a child or step-child of the principal or of the principal's spouse or de facto partner is a member of the family unit if not engaged to be married and with no spouse or de facto partner, and either under 18, or 18 to 22 and dependent on the principal or on the spouse or partner, or 23 or more and dependent under reg 1.05A(1)(b), because incapacitated for work by total or partial loss of bodily or mental functions. Financial dependence alone does not carry a child of 23 or more.

Dependent under reg 1.05A(1)(a) means wholly or substantially reliant on the other person for financial support for basic needs of food, clothing and shelter, for a substantial period immediately before the time it must be shown, and relying on that person more than on any other person or source of support. Reg 1.12(2)(b) names that other person: the principal, or the principal's spouse or de facto partner.

A step-child is a child of the parent's current spouse or de facto partner, and also a child of a former spouse or de facto partner who is under 18 and for whom the parent has a parenting order under the Family Law Act 1975 making the parent the person the child lives with or who is responsible for the child's care, or guardianship or custody under a Commonwealth, State, Territory or foreign law.

A dependent child of a child who is a member of the family unit is also a member (reg 1.12(2)(c)). A dependent child (reg 1.03) has no spouse, partner or engagement and is under 18, or 18 or more and dependent or incapacitated for work.

Both partners must be at least 18, and for a permanent visa the de facto relationship must have lasted 12 months ending immediately before the application, unless the applicant shows compelling and compassionate circumstances or the relationship is registered within s 2E of the Acts Interpretation Act (under a prescribed State or Territory law); registration waives only the 12 months, not the age 18. Section 5CB of the Act also needs a mutual commitment to a shared life, a genuine and continuing relationship and not living apart permanently.

A spouse needs a marriage valid for the Migration Act and a genuine, continuing relationship, living together or not apart permanently (s 5F). A foreign marriage is recognised under Part VA of the Marriage Act without s 88E (Migration Act s 12), so not if either party was then in another marriage recognised in Australia, not if a party domiciled in Australia was under marriageable age, not while either is under 16 when neither was domiciled here, not while voidable under the local law, and not in a prohibited relationship or without real consent.

Family members apply combined with the primary applicant, before it is decided (item 1137 note, (4A)(d)). A spouse, de facto partner or dependent child can be added by written request and payment of the additional applicant charge; that application is made on the later of the two and must then meet the whereabouts rules and time-of-application criteria (reg 2.08A). A child born to an applicant before the decision is taken to have applied at birth (reg 2.08). Non-applying family members must meet criteria 4001, 4002, 4003, 4003B and 4004, and 4005 unless unreasonable (189.211(9), 189.225(3)).

Part 189 has 3 streams. The New Zealand stream took primary applications only before 2022-12-10. The Hong Kong stream needs an application from 2022-03-05, a Hong Kong or British National (Overseas) passport, a subclass 457, 482 or 485 visa of the kind in item 1137(4M), held for at least 4 years, and 4 years of continuous usual residence before the application. A primary applicant in the Points-tested stream must not nominate the New Zealand stream.

Further criteria apply: a holder of a subclass 491 or 494 visa, or one whose last substantive visa was one, must have held it for at least 3 years at application unless an instrument's circumstances apply (189.224A); an applicant may be in or outside Australia but not in immigration clearance, and one in Australia must hold a substantive visa or a Bridging A, B or C visa (item 1137(4A)); and the public interest and special return criteria of 189.211, 189.212, 189.225 and 189.226 for the applicant and family.

The visa is permanent, but it permits travel to and entry into Australia only for 5 years from the grant (189.511), and an applicant outside Australia at grant must make first entry before the date the Minister specifies; a secondary applicant outside Australia at grant may also get condition 8515 (189.611).

The latest compiled text when read was compilation 289 of 2026-10-02; the amending regulations commencing on 2026-11-01, 2026-11-03 and 2026-11-12 (F2026L01448, F2026L01466, F2026L01449) were not compiled yet; they touch tribunal review fees and bridging, referred stay and training visas, not item 1137 or Part 189. The register's versions list names registered amendments, including ones not yet commenced, before they are compiled; an amendment newer than the compilation is only in the amending instrument.
